answer: Stake-backed identity bonding curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock fungible collateral in an escrow contract that slashes funds upon provable protocol equivocation. Attackers incur the verifiable capital cost of immobilizing liquid assets per identity, whether running agents to monitor dune shifting, route island cargo, or trade crystal oscillators. However, well-funded adversaries can still buy multiple identities linearly, biasing governance toward wealthy holders.
